name: s5-boss-plain-english
label: EXAMPLE · AI STAND-IN VOICE · NO FACE

lines.say: Your boss is about to ask your Power BI data questions in plain English.
In Microsoft Fabric, the thing that answers is a data agent.
You point it at up to five sources: semantic models, a warehouse, a KQL database.
lines.tts: You point it at up to five sources: semantic models, a warehouse, a K Q L database.

lines.say: It turns the question into DAX, SQL or KQL, runs it, and answers.
lines.tts: It turns the question into DAX, S Q L or K Q L, runs it, and answers.

lines.say: And you can publish it to Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, or any AI app that speaks MCP.
lines.tts: And you can publish it to Teams, Microsoft three sixty five Copilot, Copilot Studio, or any AI app that speaks M C P.

lines.say: Which means the semantic model you built for reports is now what the AI reads.
lines.show: Your semantic model is *what the AI reads*.

lines.say: Three catches before you demo it.
lines.title: CATCHES

lines.say: One: it's read-only. It answers questions; it doesn't change data.
lines.title: READ-ONLY
lines.sub: it answers; it doesn't change data

lines.say: Two: it answers in English, and it isn't on the free trial.
lines.title: ENGLISH, NO TRIAL

lines.say: Three: every question uses capacity. Microsoft's own example question costs about 400 CU-seconds, so watch the bill.
lines.title: IT USES CAPACITY
lines.sub: billed by tokens · ~400 CU-seconds in Microsoft's example
lines.tts: Three: every question uses capacity. Microsoft's own example question costs about four hundred C U seconds, so watch the bill.

lines.say: The skill that matters now is a clean semantic model, because that's what the AI is reading.
lines.show: The skill now: a *clean semantic model*.

lines.say: Follow, and next I'll build one live.
